metadata.title: Dual Action - Tablet + Spray
metadata.label: 6 months
metadata.subtitle: Finasteride 1mg tablet + Minoxidil 5% spray
metadata.banner: 94% experience an improvement in hair loss¹

moreInformation.title: Description
moreInformation.content:
This combination pairs two licensed treatments for male pattern hair loss that work in different ways:

  • Finasteride 1mg tablets: A medicine that reduces DHT (dihydrotestosterone), a hormone involved in hair loss.
  • Minoxidil 5% solution: A topical treatment applied to the scalp that increases blood supply to hair follicles.

The Patient Information Leaflet (PIL) for Minoxidil can be found here.

The Patient Information Leaflet (PIL) for Finasteride can be found here.

moreInformation.title: Ingredients
moreInformation.content:
Finasteride 1mg tablets

Active ingredient: Finasteride 1mg.

Excipients (inactive ingredients): Lactose monohydrate, maize starch pregelatinised, docusate sodium, iron oxide yellow (E172), sodium starch glycolate (type A), microcrystalline cellulose, colloidal anhydrous silica, magnesium stearate, purified water, hydroxypropyl cellulose, hypromellose, talc, titanium dioxide (E171), iron oxide red (E172) and iron oxide yellow (E172).

Minoxidil 5% solution

Active ingredient: Minoxidil 5% w/v.

Excipients (inactive ingredients): Ethanol 96%, propylene glycol and purified water.

moreInformation.title: Directions
moreInformation.content:
Finasteride 1mg tablets

  • Take 1 tablet once daily, with or without food.
  • Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush or break the tablet.
  • If you miss a dose, take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take a double dose.

Minoxidil 5% solution

  • Use the pump to apply 1ml of solution to the scalp each morning and night.
  • Apply only to a dry scalp.
  • Wash your hands after application.
  • Allow the solution to dry completely before using other hair products or going to bed.
  • Avoid washing your hair for at least 4 hours after application.
  • If you miss an application, continue with the next scheduled dose. Do not apply extra solution.
  • This medicine is for external use on the scalp only.
  • Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, or broken or irritated skin.
  • Avoid inhaling the spray during application.
  • If accidentally swallowed, seek urgent medical advice.

You must continue to use both medicines consistently for the treatment to work.

moreInformation.title: FAQS
moreInformation.content:
How effective is finasteride and minoxidil?

Finasteride and minoxidil are two of the most commonly used treatments for male pattern hair loss. They work in different ways and may be used together when clinically appropriate.

In one 12‑month randomised study involving 450 men with male pattern hair loss (Hu et al., Dermatologic Therapy, 2015), a higher proportion of patients experienced improvement when finasteride and minoxidil were used together compared with either treatment alone. Individual results varied, and not all patients responded to treatment.

Hair growth is gradual and it may take several months before any improvement becomes noticeable. Continued treatment is usually required to maintain any benefits.

How long does it take to work?

The treatment begins working when you start using it, but visible results may not be noticed for between 3 and 9 months.

You will usually need to take finasteride and minoxidil continuously for at least 6 to 12 months before assessing whether it is working for you. Continued treatment is required to maintain any benefits. If treatment is stopped, hair loss will generally begin to return over time.

Can I use minoxidil with finasteride?

Yes. Many men use minoxidil alongside finasteride. If clinically appropriate, combination treatment may provide additional benefit compared with either treatment alone.

Why am I shedding more hair when I start treatment?

Temporary increased shedding can occur during the first few weeks or months of treatment. This is a recognised effect of minoxidil and is usually temporary as the hair growth cycle adjusts.

Is minoxidil and finasteride suitable for everyone?

No. This treatment is intended for men aged 18 years and over with male pattern hair loss.

Minoxidil may not be suitable if you:

  • Are allergic to any of the ingredients.
  • Have high blood pressure or a heart condition.
  • Have an infected, irritated or inflamed scalp.
  • Have psoriasis or sunburn affecting the scalp.
  • Have a dressing or bandage on the scalp.
  • Have a fully shaved scalp.

Do not take finasteride if you:

  • Are allergic to finasteride or any of the ingredients.
  • Are a woman.
  • Are already taking finasteride or dutasteride for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
  • Your partner is trying to become pregnant.

Is minoxidil toxic to pets?

Yes. Minoxidil can be highly toxic to cats and may also be harmful to other pets. Store the product safely and prevent pets from contacting the product, treated scalp areas or contaminated bedding and fabrics.

Can finasteride affect fertility or sexual function?

Yes. Finasteride can cause sexual side effects in some men, including reduced sex drive (libido), erectile dysfunction and problems with ejaculation.

Some patients have reported sexual side effects that continued after treatment was stopped. The MHRA has also advised that sexual dysfunction may contribute to mood-related symptoms in some people.

Finasteride has been associated with low mood, depression and suicidal thoughts. If you experience any changes in your mood, mental wellbeing or sexual function while taking finasteride, speak to your healthcare professional.

Finasteride has also been associated with reduced semen quality and fertility problems in some men. Available evidence suggests these effects are generally reversible after discontinuing treatment.

Does finasteride cause depression?

Finasteride has been associated with depression, suicidal thoughts and sexual dysfunction.

Depression may include feelings of low self-esteem, loss of interest in activities, hopelessness, tiredness, headaches and disturbed sleep patterns.

If you develop suicidal thoughts, stop taking finasteride immediately and seek urgent medical help. If you require urgent help call 111, 999 or attend A&E.

moreInformation.title: Warnings
moreInformation.content:
Important MHRA safety information for finasteride

  • The MHRA has highlighted reports of psychiatric side effects and sexual dysfunction in patients taking finasteride.
  • Finasteride has been associated with depressed mood, depression, suicidal thoughts and sexual dysfunction.
  • Sexual side effects may include reduced sex drive, erectile dysfunction and ejaculation disorders.
  • Some patients have reported sexual side effects that continued after stopping treatment.
  • You will be provided with a Patient Information Leaflet and a Finasteride Patient Card. Please read both.
  • Tell your clinician before starting treatment if you have a personal history of depression, low mood or suicidal thoughts.
  • If you experience sexual dysfunction while taking finasteride, contact your healthcare professional.
  • If you develop depressed mood, depression or suicidal thoughts while taking finasteride, stop treatment and contact a healthcare professional as soon as possible.
  • If you feel at risk of harming yourself, or have seriously harmed yourself, call 999 or seek emergency medical help immediately.

Keep minoxidil solution away from pets

Minoxidil can be highly toxic to cats and may also harm other pets. Store it securely and keep pets away from the product, your treated scalp and any bedding or fabric it may have touched.

Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting treatment if:

  • You are allergic to finasteride, minoxidil or any ingredient in either product.
  • You are female.
  • You are under 18 years old.
  • You are already taking finasteride or dutasteride for a prostate condition.
  • You are using any other medicine on your scalp.
  • You have a dressing or bandage on your scalp.
  • You have sudden or uneven hair loss, total baldness, or unexplained hair loss.
  • You have a scalp condition such as psoriasis, sunburn, damaged skin, redness, inflammation or scalp pain.
  • You have signs of cardiovascular disease, a heart rhythm problem or high blood pressure.
  • You are due to have a PSA blood test.

Pregnancy and fertility

  • Finasteride should not be taken by women.
  • Women who are pregnant or trying to become pregnant should not handle crushed or broken finasteride tablets.
  • Whole coated tablets can be handled normally.
  • If contact occurs with a crushed or broken tablet during pregnancy, seek medical advice.
  • Infertility has been reported in some men taking long-term finasteride. Semen quality generally improves after stopping treatment.

Stop treatment and contact a doctor if you experience:

  • Signs of an allergic reaction, including swelling of the lips, face, tongue or throat, difficulty swallowing, hives or difficulty breathing. Seek urgent medical attention immediately.
  • Depression or feelings of severe sadness, hopelessness or worthlessness.
  • Breast lumps, pain, enlargement or nipple discharge.
  • Low blood pressure, chest pain, a faster heartbeat, weakness, dizziness, sudden unexplained weight gain, swollen hands or feet, or persistent scalp irritation.
  • Any other unexpected new symptom.

Possible side effects of finasteride

Uncommon (up to 1 in 100 people):

  • Difficulty getting or keeping an erection.
  • Reduced desire for sex.
  • Changes in ejaculation, including reduced semen volume.

Not known (frequency cannot be estimated):

  • Breast swelling or tenderness.
  • Testicular pain.
  • Blood in semen.
  • Palpitations.
  • Persistent erectile, libido or ejaculation problems after stopping treatment.
  • Male infertility and/or reduced semen quality.
  • Changes in liver function seen on blood tests.
  • Anxiety.
  • Suicidal thoughts.

Possible side effects of minoxidil 5% solution

Very common (more than 1 in 10 people):

  • Headache.

Common (up to 1 in 10 people):

  • Itching.
  • Increased hair growth beyond the scalp.
  • Skin reactions including acne-like rash.
  • Shortness of breath.
  • Swollen arms and legs.
  • Weight gain.
  • High blood pressure.
  • Scalp irritation including stinging, burning, dryness, itching, scaling or inflamed hair follicles.

Uncommon (up to 1 in 100 people):

  • Dizziness.
  • Nausea.

Rare (up to 1 in 1,000 people):

  • Change in hair texture.

If any side effect becomes serious, or you notice a side effect not listed here, speak to your doctor or pharmacist.

usps: Can slow or promote hair regrowth in some men
Treatment only available following clinical suitability

metadata.title: Finasteride tablets
metadata.label: 1 month
metadata.subtitle: Finasteride 1mg tablet
metadata.banner: 83% experience an improvement in hair loss²

moreInformation.title: Description
moreInformation.content:
Finasteride 1 mg tablets contain the active substance finasteride, a prescription medicine used to treat male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) in adult men.

Finasteride works by reducing levels of a hormone called dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which is associated with male pattern hair loss. This can help increase hair growth on the scalp and prevent further hair loss in men.

Men with mild to moderate, but not complete, hair loss may benefit from treatment with finasteride.

Finasteride should only be used by adult men and should be taken exactly as prescribed.

The finasteride patient information leaflet can be found here.

moreInformation.title: Ingredients
moreInformation.content:
Excipients (inactive ingredients): The inactive ingredients in finasteride tablets may vary depending on the manufacturer. Patients should refer to the patient information leaflet supplied with their medicine for the full list of ingredients.

Examples of inactive ingredients that may be included are:

Tablet core: Lactose monohydrate, microcrystalline cellulose, sodium starch glycolate, pregelatinised maize starch, docusate sodium, and magnesium stearate.

Tablet coat: Hypromellose, hydroxypropyl cellulose, talc, titanium dioxide (E171), red iron oxide (E172), and yellow iron oxide (E172).

If you have an allergy or intolerance to any ingredient, including lactose, speak to your healthcare professional before taking this medicine.

moreInformation.title: Directions
moreInformation.content:
Take 1 tablet once daily, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet.

If you forget to take a dose, take your next dose at the usual time. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed dose.

It is important to continue taking finasteride as prescribed for the treatment to be effective. Hair growth may take several months to become noticeable, and continued treatment is usually required to maintain any benefits.

If you have any questions about how to take this medicine, speak to your healthcare professional.

moreInformation.title: FAQS
moreInformation.content:
How does this treatment work?

Finasteride works by blocking the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone that contributes to male pattern hair loss. By reducing DHT levels in the scalp, finasteride may help slow further hair loss and support hair regrowth in some men.

How long does it take to work?

You will usually need to take finasteride continuously for at least 6 to 12 months before assessing whether it is working for you. Some men may notice improvements sooner, but individual results can vary.

Continued treatment is required to maintain any benefits. If treatment is stopped, hair loss will generally begin to return over time.

Will the effects last if I stop treatment?

No. If treatment is stopped, the beneficial effects of finasteride generally begin to reverse within several months, and hair loss may gradually return to pre-treatment levels.

Who can take finasteride?

Finasteride is used for the treatment of male pattern hair loss in adult men. It is not suitable for everyone, and some people may need to avoid this medicine or discuss its use with a healthcare professional before starting treatment.

Do not take finasteride:

moreInformation.title: Warnings
moreInformation.content:
Important MHRA safety information

The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has highlighted reports of psychiatric side effects and sexual dysfunction in patients taking finasteride.

  • Finasteride has been associated with depressed mood, depression, suicidal thoughts, and sexual dysfunction.
  • Sexual side effects may include reduced sex drive (libido), erectile dysfunction, and ejaculation disorders.
  • Some patients have reported sexual side effects that continued after stopping treatment.
  • The MHRA advises patients to read the Patient Information Leaflet and any patient safety information supplied with the medicine.
  • Tell your healthcare professional before starting treatment if you have a personal history of depression, low mood, or suicidal thoughts.
  • If you experience sexual dysfunction while taking finasteride, contact your healthcare professional for advice.
  • If you develop depressed mood, depression, or suicidal thoughts while taking finasteride, stop treatment and contact a healthcare professional as soon as possible.
  • If you feel at risk of harming yourself or have seriously harmed yourself, call 999 or seek emergency medical assistance immediately
 

Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking finasteride if:

  • You are due to have a blood test for prostate-specific antigen (PSA). Finasteride can affect PSA test results, so your healthcare professional should be aware that you are taking this medicine.

Other important warnings

  • Infertility has been reported in some men taking finasteride, particularly in those with other risk factors that may affect fertility.
  • Improvement or normalisation of semen quality has been reported after stopping finasteride.
  • Long-term clinical studies investigating the effects of finasteride on male fertility have not been conducted.
  • Finasteride should not be taken by women.
  • Women who are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are planning a pregnancy should not handle crushed or broken finasteride tablets. Whole tablets are coated to prevent contact with the active ingredient during normal use.
  • Exposure during pregnancy may affect the development of a male baby’s sex organs.
  • If a pregnant woman comes into contact with crushed or broken finasteride tablets, medical advice should be sought.

Stop taking finasteride and seek medical advice immediately if you experience:

  • Symptoms of an allergic reaction, including swelling of the lips, face, tongue, or throat, difficulty swallowing, hives (raised itchy rash), or difficulty breathing.
  • Depression, severe low mood, or thoughts of self-harm or suicide.

You should promptly report any changes in breast tissue to your healthcare professional, including breast lumps, pain, enlargement, tenderness, or nipple discharge, as these may be signs of a serious condition such as breast cancer.

Possible side effects

Uncommon side effects (may affect up to 1 in 100 people)

  • Reduced sex drive (libido).
  • Difficulty achieving or maintaining an erection (erectile dysfunction).
  • Problems with ejaculation, including a decrease in the amount of semen released during sex.

The reduction in semen volume does not appear to affect normal sexual function.

Frequency not known (cannot be estimated from available data)

  • Breast swelling or breast tenderness.
  • Pain in the testicles.
  • Blood in the semen.
  • Palpitations (awareness of your heartbeat).
  • Persistent difficulty achieving or maintaining an erection after stopping treatment.
  • Persistent reduction in sex drive after stopping treatment.
  • Persistent ejaculation problems after stopping treatment.
  • Male infertility and/or poor semen quality.
  • Changes in liver function, which may be detected through blood tests.
  • Anxiety.
  • Suicidal thoughts.

If any side effect becomes serious, or if you notice any side effects not listed in the patient information leaflet, tell your doctor, pharmacist, or other healthcare professional. It may be helpful to make a note of what happened, when it started, and how long it lasted.

Please read the patient information leaflet supplied with your medicine for the complete list of warnings, precautions, and side effects.

usps: Lowers DHT, the hormone behind hair loss

metadata.title: Sons Minoxidil spray
metadata.label: 6 months
metadata.subtitle: Minoxidil 5% spray

moreInformation.title: Description
moreInformation.content:
Sons Minoxidil 5% Solution, Spray contains minoxidil, one of the few clinically established medicines used to treat male pattern hair loss.

It is applied directly to affected areas of the scalp and works by increasing the supply of blood and nutrients to hair follicles. This helps stimulate hair growth and may slow the process of hair loss.

The patient information leaflet can be found here.

moreInformation.title: Ingredients
moreInformation.content:
Active ingredient: Minoxidil 5% w/v.

Excipients (inactive ingredients): ethanol 96%, propylene glycol and purified water.

moreInformation.title: Directions
moreInformation.content:
The solution comes in a small bottle with a pump. Use the pump to apply 1ml of the solution to your scalp each morning and night.

It is important to apply it only to dry scalp and wash your hands after use.

Allow the solution to dry completely before using other hair products or going to bed, and avoid washing your hair for at least 4 hours after application.

It is important to use Minoxidil consistently, as this helps maintain its effect.

If you miss a dose, take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take a double dose.

  • If you miss an application, continue with the next scheduled dose. Do not apply extra solution.
  • If accidentally swallowed, seek urgent medical advice.
  • This medicine is for external use on the scalp only.
  • Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, or broken or irritated skin.
  • Avoid inhaling the spray during application.

You must continue to use Minoxidil 5% for the treatment to work.

moreInformation.title: FAQS
moreInformation.content:
How effective is Minoxidil 5% Spray?

Clinical studies have shown that many men experience improvement in their hair loss while using minoxidil consistently. In one study, 71% showed improved hair density over 16 weeks and in another study, 84% of patients found the treatment effective over 52 weeks. Individual results vary, and not everyone will respond to treatment.

How long does it take to work?

The treatment begins working when you start using it, but visible results may not be noticed for between 3 and 9 months.

You will usually need to use Minoxidil continuously for at least 6 to 12 months before assessing whether it is working for you. Continued treatment is required to maintain any benefits. If treatment is stopped, hair loss will generally begin to return over time.

Can I use Minoxidil with Finasteride?

Yes. Many men use Minoxidil alongside Finasteride. If clinically appropriate, combination treatment may provide additional benefit compared with either treatment alone.

Why am I shedding more hair when I start treatment?

Temporary increased shedding can occur during the first few weeks or months of treatment. This is a recognised effect of minoxidil and is usually temporary as the hair growth cycle adjusts.

Is Minoxidil suitable for everyone?

No. Minoxidil is intended for men aged 18 years and over with male pattern hair loss and may not be suitable if you:

  • are allergic to any of the ingredients
  • have high blood pressure or a heart condition
  • have an infected, irritated or inflamed scalp
  • have psoriasis or sunburn affecting the scalp
  • have a dressing or bandage on the scalp
  • have a fully shaved scalp

Is Minoxidil toxic to pets?

Yes. Minoxidil can be highly toxic to cats and may also be harmful to other pets. Store the product safely and prevent pets from contacting the product, treated scalp areas or contaminated bedding and fabrics.

moreInformation.title: Warnings
moreInformation.content:
Keep away from pets, particularly cats, as accidental exposure can be serious or fatal.

Do not use Minoxidil:

  • if you are allergic to minoxidil or any of the other ingredients of this medicine
  • if you are a female
  • if you are under the age of 18 or over the age of 65
  • if you are using any other medicines on the scalp
  • if you have any kind of dressing or bandage on your scalp
  • if you suffer from sudden or uneven hair loss
  • if you have any condition that affects your scalp, including psoriasis (an itchy inflammatory skin condition), sunburn, shaved scalp, or if your scalp skin is damaged by scars or burns, since no hair roots are present
  • if you have total baldness or complete loss of all body hair
  • if you have any signs of cardiovascular disease or heart rhythm problems
  • if you suffer from high blood pressure
  • if you have a red, inflamed or painful scalp
  • if you do not know why you are losing your hair
  • if you are not sure if your hair loss is hereditary

You should stop Minoxidil and consult a doctor if:

  • you are found to have low blood pressure
  • you develop chest pain, a faster heartbeat, weakness or dizziness
  • you experience sudden and unexplained weight gain
  • you develop swollen hands or feet
  • you have persistent redness or irritation of the scalp
  • you experience any other unexpected new symptoms

Possible side effects

Very common (may affect more than 1 in 10 people):

  • headache

Common (may affect up to 1 in 10 people):

  • itching
  • increased hair growth beyond the scalp (including facial hair growth in women)
  • inflammatory skin reactions, including acneiform rash and skin rash
  • shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
  • swollen arms and legs
  • weight gain
  • high blood pressure
  • irritation of the scalp such as stinging, burning, dryness, itching, scaling, or infected and inflamed hair follicles

Uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people):

  • dizziness
  • nausea

Rare (may affect up to 1 in 1,000 people):

  • change in hair texture. If this happens, you should stop using Minoxidil.

metadata.title: Propecia
metadata.label: 1 month
metadata.subtitle: Finasteride 1mg tablet
metadata.banner: 83% experience an improvement in hair loss²

moreInformation.title: Description
moreInformation.content:
Propecia 1mg tablets contain finasteride, a prescription medicine used to treat male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) in adult men.

Propecia increases hair growth on the scalp and prevents further hair loss in men. Men with mild to moderate, but not complete hair loss, can benefit from using Propecia.

The patient information leaflet can be found here.

moreInformation.title: Ingredients
moreInformation.content:
Active ingredient: Finasteride 1mg.

Excipients (inactive ingredients): lactose, microcrystalline cellulose E460, pregelatinized maize starch, sodium starch glycollate, docusate sodium, magnesium stearate E572, hypromellose E464, hydroxypropyl cellulose E463, titanium dioxide, talc, yellow iron oxide E172, red iron oxide E172.

moreInformation.title: Directions
moreInformation.content:
Take 1 tablet once daily, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush or break the tablet.

If you miss a dose, take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take a double dose.

You must continue to take Propecia for the treatment to work.

moreInformation.title: FAQS
moreInformation.content:
How does this treatment work?

Propecia works by blocking the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone that contributes to male pattern hair loss. By lowering DHT levels in the scalp, Propecia may help reduce further hair loss and support hair regrowth in some men.

How long does it take to work?

You will usually need to take Propecia continuously for at least 6 to 12 months before assessing whether it is working for you. Continued treatment is required to maintain any benefits. If treatment is stopped, hair loss will generally begin to return over time.

Will the effects last if I stop treatment?

No. If treatment is stopped, the beneficial effects generally begin to reverse within several months and hair loss may gradually return to pre-treatment levels.

Who can take Propecia?

Propecia is for the treatment of male pattern hair loss in men only. Exceptions include those whose partner is trying to get pregnant, and those with certain health conditions or taking specific medications.

Do not take Propecia:

  • if you are allergic (hypersensitive) to finasteride (Propecia) or any of the other ingredients of this medicine.
  • if you are a woman (because this medicine is for men). It has been shown in clinical trials that Propecia does not work in women with hair loss.
  • if you are already taking finasteride or dutasteride used for a prostate problem called benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

Can Propecia affect fertility or sexual function?

Yes. Propecia can cause sexual side effects in some men, including reduced sex drive (libido), erectile dysfunction and problems with ejaculation.

moreInformation.title: Warnings
moreInformation.content:
Important MHRA safety information about finasteride (Propecia)

  • The MHRA has highlighted reports of psychiatric side effects and sexual dysfunction in patients taking finasteride.
  • Finasteride has been associated with depressed mood, depression, suicidal thoughts and sexual dysfunction.
  • Sexual side effects may include reduced sex drive, erectile dysfunction and ejaculation disorders.
  • Some patients have reported sexual side effects that continued after stopping treatment.
  • The MHRA advises patients to read the Patient Information Leaflet and Finasteride Patient Card supplied with the medicine.
  • Tell your clinician before starting treatment if you have a personal history of depression, low mood or suicidal thoughts.
  • If you experience sexual dysfunction while taking finasteride, contact your healthcare professional for advice.
  • If you develop depressed mood, depression or suicidal thoughts while taking finasteride 1mg for male pattern hair loss, stop treatment and contact a healthcare professional as soon as possible.
  • If you feel at risk of harming yourself or have seriously harmed yourself, call 999 or seek emergency medical assistance immediately.

Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Propecia if:

  • You are going to have a blood test for prostate cancer called PSA (prostate-specific antigen). This is because Propecia can affect the result of this test.

Other warnings:

  • Infertility has been reported in men who took Propecia for a long time and had other risk factors that may affect fertility. Normalisation or improvement of seminal quality has been reported after discontinuation of Propecia. Long-term clinical studies about the effect of Propecia on fertility in men have not been conducted.
  • Propecia should not be taken by women.
  • Do not touch crushed or broken tablets of Propecia if you are a woman who is pregnant or planning to become pregnant (whole tablets are coated to stop contact with the medicine during normal use). This is because this medicine may affect the baby’s sex organs.
  • If a woman who is pregnant comes into contact with crushed or broken Propecia tablets, speak to your doctor.

Stop taking Propecia and talk to your doctor if you experience:

  • Symptoms of an allergic reaction: swelling of your lips, face, tongue and throat; difficulty swallowing; lumps under your skin (hives) and breathing difficulties. Stop taking Propecia and talk to your doctor immediately.
  • Depression (feeling of severe sadness and unworthiness).

You should promptly report to your doctor any changes in the breast tissue such as lumps, pain, enlargement or nipple discharge as these may be signs of a serious condition, such as breast cancer.

Uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people):

  • you may be unable to have an erection (impotence)
  • you may have less desire to have sex
  • difficulty having an erection
  • you may have problems with ejaculation, for example a decrease in the amount of semen released during sex. This decrease in the amount of semen does not appear to affect normal sexual function.

Not known: frequency cannot be estimated from the available data

  • breast swelling or tenderness
  • pain in the testicles
  • blood in semen
  • palpitations (feeling your heartbeat)
  • persistent difficulty having an erection after discontinuation of treatment
  • persistent decrease in sex drive after discontinuation of treatment
  • persistent problems with ejaculation after discontinuation of treatment
  • male infertility and/or poor quality of semen
  • changes in the way your liver is working, which can be shown by a blood test
  • anxiety
  • suicidal thoughts

If any of these side effects gets serious, or if you notice any side effects not listed in the patient information leaflet, tell your doctor or pharmacist. It may help to make a note of what happened, when it started and how long it lasted.

groupMetadata.treatmentInfo: Finasteride forms the foundation of treatment by helping to protect hair follicles from DHT, the hormone responsible for male pattern hair loss. Minoxidil complements this by stimulating growth and increasing hair density. Together, they tackle both hair loss and regrowth for a more complete approach to treatment.

Clinically proven to preserve your hair by blocking the conversion of testosterone to DHT, a chemical that shrinks hair follicles, giving hair a chance to regrow and working to prevent further hair loss.
Increases blood flow to the scalp to stimulate growth and boost hair density.
